problems.title: From counters to a diagnosis
problems.statement: A kernel: 1.2 ms, DRAM SOL 91%, L2 SOL 55%, issue SOL 40% (FMA share 15%), coalescing 25%.

parts.prompt: Estimated new time, if coalescing cuts DRAM traffic 4× and issue work is unchanged, in ms?

problems.solution: DRAM is saturated, and 75% of the bytes are wasted: fix coalescing first. If DRAM traffic falls 4×, the time bound falls to 0.3 ms, until issue (40% of 1.2 ms ≈ 0.48 ms) takes over: the estimate is max(0.3, 0.48) = 0.48 ms, now issue-bound.

problems.title: Waves
problems.statement: A 132-SM GPU, 2 resident blocks per SM. A grid of 300 equal blocks.
problems.solution: 2 waves, the second with 36 blocks: 300/528 = 57%. 264 blocks (or 528) would fit exactly; finer blocks or Stream-K remove the tail.

problems.title: Timing honestly
problems.solution: Median 40 µs; the mean (64.6) is dominated by the cold first run and one interrupted run. Report median or min after warm-up.

problems.title: Register pressure
problems.statement: 256-thread blocks; registers allocated per warp in units of 256; 65,536 per SM; 64-warp limit.

parts.prompt: Most registers per thread that still allow 4 blocks?

problems.solution: 72 × 32 = 2,304 → 28 warps → 3 blocks: 37.5%. 4 blocks need ≤ 2,048 per warp: 64 registers.

problems.title: Scheduling
problems.statement: One warp, in-order issue, latencies: ld.global 400, fma 4. Code: ld a; ld b; c = fma(a); d = fma(b); e = fma(c, d).
problems.solution: ld a at 0, ld b at 1 (ready 401); c at 400 (a ready), d at 401, e waits for d (405): done at 409. The loads were already hoisted; the remaining time is latency.

problems.title: Loop legality
problems.statement: for i: for j: a[i][j] = a[i][j−1] + a[i−1][j].

parts.prompt: Is interchanging i and j legal?
Can the inner loop run in parallel as written?

problems.solution: Distances (0, 1) and (1, 0); interchange maps them to (1, 0) and (0, 1): legal. Neither loop is parallel as is; anti-diagonals (wavefronts) are.

problems.title: Max live
problems.statement: a = ld; b = ld; c = a + b; d = c * a; e = d + b; f = e * c; f is the result.

parts.prompt: Maximum values live at once (counting the one being defined)?

problems.solution: At d's definition, a (used for the last time), b, c and d are live: 4; at e's, b, c, d and e: 4. Elsewhere 3. So 4 registers.

problems.title: Attention memory
problems.statement: Training attention, 16 heads, N = 4,096, d = 64, batch 4, FP16.

parts.prompt: GiB to store P for one layer?
GiB for Q, K, V and O together?

problems.solution: P: 2 GiB; Q, K, V, O: 0.125 GiB. FlashAttention keeps the second and recomputes the first.

problems.title: Streams
problems.statement: Upload 6 ms, compute 9 ms, download 3 ms; 2 copy engines; many chunks.

parts.prompt: With a single copy engine, ideally?

problems.solution: Serial 18; pipelined max(6, 9, 3) = 9; with one copy engine the copies total 9 ms and still fit behind 9 ms of compute: 9.

problems.title: Numerics
problems.statement: FP32 has 24 significand bits.

parts.prompt: Smallest positive integer n such that n + 1 rounds to n in FP32?
Summing 10⁸ ones in a sequential FP32 loop gives…

problems.solution: $2^{24} = 16{,}777{,}216$: above it, the spacing is 2, and +1 ties to even. The loop sticks there.

problems.title: Portability
problems.statement: Code runs on 64-wide wavefronts.
problems.solution: Hard-coded 31, 32-bit masks and a 16-offset start all assume 32 lanes; using warpSize is correct.

problems.title: Power
problems.statement: Dynamic power ∝ f³. A compute-bound kernel at f₀ uses 240 W dynamic + 60 W static and takes 10 ms.
problems.solution: (a) 300 W × 10 ms = 3.0 J. (b) (122.9 + 60) W × 12.5 ms = 2.29 J: slower but cheaper.

problems.title: Design: a fused kernel
problems.statement: Fuse y = LayerNorm(x + r) for 8192 × 1024 FP16 tensors (x, r in; y and h = x + r out) on a 1 TB/s GPU.

options: One warp per row, values in registers, two-pass statistics

problems.solution: Read x and r, write h and y: 4 × 16 MiB = 64 MiB, 67 µs. A warp per row holds 32 FP16 values per lane, computes mean and variance from registers, and writes once.

problems.statement: Exclusive scan of $2^{26}$ ints at 1 TB/s.

problems.title: Radix sort
problems.statement: Sort $2^{25}$ 32-bit keys with 32-bit values using 8-bit digits, Onesweep-style (one histogram pass over keys, then each digit pass reads and writes keys and values once).

problems.title: Tensor-core tiles
problems.statement: A GPU with a 300 FLOP/byte FP16 tensor ridge. A tiled GEMM's DRAM intensity with FP16 inputs is about T/2 for T × T block tiles.

parts.prompt: Smallest power-of-two T that is compute-bound?

options: No: such tiles don't fit on chip; L2 reuse across blocks (rasterisation) supplies the rest

problems.solution: T/2 > 300 → T > 600 → 1024, far too big for one SM. Real kernels use 128–256 tiles and rely on L2 hits across concurrently running blocks to raise the effective DRAM intensity.

options: Flush L2 if production inputs arrive cold
Report the fastest single run only

problems.solution: Everything except cherry-picking.

problems.title: Little's law and ILP
problems.statement: A GPU needs 270 KB in flight. A kernel runs 512 warps GPU-wide with 4-byte loads, one per lane.

parts.prompt: Bytes in flight with one load per warp?
Loads in flight per warp needed?

options: float4 loads plus unrolling by 2 (8× the bytes per warp)

problems.solution: 65,536 bytes; ⌈270,000/65,536⌉ = 5 loads per warp; float4 (4×) and a 2× unroll give 8×, enough without more warps.

problems.title: Compiler pipeline
problems.statement: Where does each happen?

parts.prompt: JIT for a GPU newer than the build

problems.solution: ptxas allocates; contraction appears in PTX; the driver JITs PTX for newer GPUs.
